title: Bicanonical connectedness and finite covers of numerical Godeaux surfaces
accepted_claim: For a numerical Godeaux surface, every bicanonical member is 2-connected if and only if Picard torsion is zero. These conditions imply integral H_1=0 and no nontrivial finite quotient or connected finite cover; the profinite completion and algebraic fundamental group are trivial.

scope.surface: Smooth, connected, minimal complex projective surface of general type with p_g=q=0 and K^2=1.
scope.quantifier: Every member of the complete bicanonical pencil; decompositions may have repeated or shared components.
scope.four_base_points: Four distinct simple base points remain a hypothesis of the unresolved target; they are unnecessary for the accepted deductions.
scope.finite_cover_bound: Every connected finite unramified topological cover of any numerical Godeaux surface has degree at most six.
scope.conditional_topological_conclusion: Topological simple connectivity follows if the fundamental group is finite or residually finite; neither condition is established.
scope.source_typo: In the inspected arXiv:2201.12065v1 proof of Lemma 2.1 the displayed cross term misses a factor 2. The correct identity is D_1^2+D_2^2=4-2D_1.D_2. This remains sufficient there, and the authored proof is independent of that expansion.

remaining_target_gaps: Exclude or construct an infinite, finitely presented, perfect topological fundamental group with no nontrivial finite quotient and no proper finite-index subgroup for a smooth numerical Godeaux surface with four distinct simple bicanonical base points and every bicanonical member 2-connected.
question_credit: Miles Reid, Attempt to construct the general simply connected Godeaux surface, Oberwolfach Report 27/2006, printed pp.1645-1647.
